title: Invoice Verification & FI Integration
intro: How MM postings reach the general ledger automatically, how invoices are matched and blocked, and how the GR/IR account is managed.
objectives: Explain automatic account determination and the main transaction keys
Predict the accounting entries for GR and invoice with price control S and V
Post, park and correct invoices in MIRO
Handle tolerances, blocked invoices and GR/IR clearing

lessons.title: Automatic account determination
lessons.body:
MM users never enter G/L accounts for stock movements. The system finds them automatically using:

  • Chart of accounts (from the company code)
  • Valuation grouping code (from the plant/valuation area)
  • Transaction key (from the movement type)
  • Account modifier (refines some keys)
  • Valuation class (from the material master)

Configured in OBYC (FI/MM consultants); simulate with OMWB.

Main transaction keys

KeyAccount
BSXInventory (stock) account
WRXGR/IR clearing account
PRDPrice differences
GBBOffsetting entry for inventory posting, e.g. consumption (modifier VBR), scrapping (VNG), inventory differences (INV)
KBSAccount-assigned purchases (e.g. cost centre)

As a trainer you don't configure OBYC, but explaining “valuation class + movement type = G/L account” wins over finance teams in class.
lessons.narration: MM users never type a general ledger account for a stock movement. The system finds the account automatically, using a few ingredients: the chart of accounts, from the company code; the valuation grouping code, from the plant; the transaction key, from the movement type; sometimes an account modifier; and the valuation class, from the material master. This is configured in O B Y C, usually by consultants, and you can simulate it with O M W B. The transaction keys to know are: B S X, the inventory account; W R X, the G R I R clearing account; P R D, price differences; G B B, the offsetting entry for inventory postings, for example consumption, scrapping, or inventory differences, distinguished by an account modifier; and K B S, for account-assigned purchases such as a cost centre. As a trainer, you won't configure O B Y C. But being able to say that valuation class plus movement type equals general ledger account will win over any finance team in your class.
keyTerms: Offsetting entry for inventory postings (consumption, scrapping…)

tryIt.task: Display the accounting document of a GR (MIGO → Doc. info → FI documents) and identify the inventory and GR/IR accounts.
If you have access, run OMWB to simulate account determination for movement type 101 and your material.

lessons.title: GR/IR and price differences: S vs V
lessons.body:
Example

PO for 10 units at €12. Material standard price: €10.

Price control S (standard price)

StepDebitCredit
GRInventory (BSX) 100 + Price diff. (PRD) 20GR/IR (WRX) 120
Invoice at €12GR/IR 120Supplier 120
Invoice at €13 insteadGR/IR 120 + PRD 10Supplier 130

Stock always stays at the standard price; every difference goes to PRD.

Price control V (moving average)

StepDebitCredit
GRInventory 120GR/IR 120
Invoice at €13 (stock still on hand)GR/IR 120 + Inventory 10Supplier 130

The difference goes to stock and the moving average price changes. If the stock has already been consumed, the difference goes to PRD instead.

GR/IR: the waiting room

  • Credited at GR, debited at invoice
  • A balance means goods received but not invoiced, or invoiced but not received
  • Analyse with MB5S; clear old differences with MR11

Work through this example on paper with learners before showing the system. Then MIRO results stop being a mystery.
lessons.narration: Let's work through an example. A purchase order for ten units at twelve euros each, for a material with a standard price of ten euros. With price control S, standard price, stock is always valued at the standard price. At goods receipt, inventory is debited one hundred, the price difference account is debited twenty, and G R I R is credited one hundred and twenty. If the invoice comes in at twelve euros, G R I R is debited one hundred and twenty and the supplier credited the same. If instead the invoice says thirteen euros, the extra ten goes to price differences too. Now with price control V, moving average price. At goods receipt, inventory is debited one hundred and twenty, at the purchase order price, and G R I R credited one hundred and twenty. If the invoice says thirteen euros, and the stock is still on hand, the extra ten goes to inventory, and the moving average price goes up. If the stock has already been consumed, the difference goes to price differences instead. And the G R I R account? Think of it as a waiting room: credited at goods receipt, debited at invoice. A balance means goods received but not invoiced, or invoiced but not received. Work through this example on paper with learners before you show the system, and invoice postings stop being a mystery.
keyTerms: Difference between PO/invoice price and standard price → PRD
Invoice differences adjust stock value if stock is on hand

tryIt.task: For a material with price control S, create a PO at a price different from the standard price, post the GR and find the PRD line in the accounting document.
Repeat with a V material and check the moving average price in MM03 before and after.

lessons.title: MIRO in practice
lessons.body:
Header

  • Transaction: Invoice, Credit memo, Subsequent debit, Subsequent credit
  • Invoice date, posting date, reference (supplier's invoice number), amount, tax code / Calculate tax
  • Payment tab: terms, due date, payment block; Details tab: invoicing party, unplanned delivery costs

Reference

  • Purchase order/scheduling agreement, delivery note, bill of lading, supplier
  • Layout: goods/service items, planned delivery costs, or both

Parking vs posting

  • Park (MIR7 or Save as parked): saves without accounting; someone else can complete or approve
  • Post: creates invoice and accounting documents

Corrections

  • Credit memo: supplier credits goods returned or overbilled (quantity-related)
  • Subsequent debit/credit: price correction only, no quantity change
  • Cancel a posted invoice with MR8M

Display

MIR4 display invoice, MIR5 invoice list. Fiori: Manage Supplier Invoices, Supplier Invoices List.

The difference between credit memo and subsequent credit is a guaranteed exam question.
lessons.narration: In M I R O, the header starts with the transaction: invoice, credit memo, subsequent debit, or subsequent credit. Then the invoice date, posting date, the reference, which is the supplier's invoice number, the amount and the tax code. The payment tab holds terms, due date and payment block. Below the header, you choose the reference document, usually the purchase order, but it can also be a delivery note or bill of lading. You can either park or post an invoice. Parking, also done with M I R seven, saves it without any accounting entries, so someone else can complete or approve it. Posting creates the invoice document and the accounting document. For corrections: a credit memo is used when the supplier credits goods returned or overbilled, and it's quantity-related. A subsequent debit or subsequent credit corrects the price only, without changing the quantity. And to reverse a posted invoice, use M R eight M. Display an invoice with M I R four, and list invoices with M I R five. Remember this one: the difference between a credit memo and a subsequent credit is a guaranteed exam question.

tryIt.task: Park an invoice for one of your POs, then complete and post it.
Post a subsequent debit of €20 on the same PO item and check the PO history.
Cancel the subsequent debit with MR8M.

lessons.title: Tolerances, blocking and release
lessons.body:
Tolerance keys

Configured per company code (OMR6). Common ones:

KeyChecks
PPPrice variance
DQQuantity variance (invoiced more than received)
DWQuantity variance when GR quantity is zero
STDate variance
BDSmall differences posted automatically

Blocking reasons

If a tolerance is exceeded, the invoice still posts but is blocked for payment (payment block R).

  • Price, quantity, date, quality blocks
  • Manual block: set on the item
  • Stochastic block: random checks above a threshold

Releasing

  • MRBR release blocked invoices: manually, or automatically when the reason disappears (e.g. the missing GR is posted)
  • Fiori: Manage Supplier Invoices with blocked filter

Duplicate check

Same supplier + reference + amount + date triggers a warning or error, if check double invoice is active.

Real accounts payable teams spend hours in MRBR. A trainer who explains why an invoice is blocked saves them days.
lessons.narration: Invoices are checked against tolerances, configured per company code. The common tolerance keys are: P P, for price variance; D Q, for quantity variance, when more is invoiced than received; D W, for quantity variance when nothing has been received yet; S T, for date variance; and B D, which lets small differences be posted automatically. If a tolerance is exceeded, the invoice still posts, but it's blocked for payment, with payment block R. Blocks can be for price, quantity, date or quality. There are also manual blocks, set by the user on an item, and stochastic blocks, random checks on invoices above a threshold. To release blocked invoices, use M R B R. It can release them manually, or automatically once the reason disappears, for example when the missing goods receipt is finally posted. There's also a duplicate check: if the same supplier, reference, amount and date appear twice, the system warns you, provided check double invoice is active on the supplier. Real accounts payable teams spend hours in M R B R. A trainer who can explain why an invoice is blocked saves them days.
keyTerms: Random check on invoices above a threshold

tryIt.task: Post an invoice at a much higher price than the PO and check that it's blocked.

lessons.title: GR/IR clearing and Evaluated Receipt Settlement
lessons.body:
GR/IR account maintenance

  • Small or permanent differences (e.g. supplier will never invoice the last unit) stay on GR/IR
  • MR11 clears them, posting to a GR/IR clearing difference account
  • MB5S lists balances to analyse
  • Month-end: GR/IR regrouping (in FI) reclassifies balances for the balance sheet

Evaluated Receipt Settlement (ERS)

  • No paper invoice: the system creates the invoice from the PO price and GR quantity
  • Requires the ERS flag in supplier purchasing data and on the PO item
  • Run with MRRL
  • Common in the automotive industry and with trusted suppliers

Other automatic settlements

  • MRKO: consignment and pipeline settlement (Module 9)
  • MRIS: invoicing plan settlement (e.g. monthly rent)

Build your invoice-matching exercise pack here: one clean invoice, one price variance, one quantity variance, one credit memo.
lessons.narration: Sometimes small or permanent differences stay on the G R I R account, for example when the supplier will never invoice the last unit. M R one one clears those, posting them to a clearing difference account, and M B five S lists balances so you can analyse them. At month-end, finance reclassifies G R I R balances for the balance sheet. Next, evaluated receipt settlement, or E R S. With E R S there's no paper invoice: the system creates the invoice itself, from the purchase order price and the goods receipt quantity. It needs the E R S flag in the supplier's purchasing data and on the purchase order item, and it's run with M R R L. It's common in the automotive industry and with trusted suppliers. Similar automatic settlements exist for consignment and pipeline, with M R K O, which we'll see in module nine, and for invoicing plans such as monthly rent, with M R I S. This is a good place to build your invoice-matching exercise pack: one clean invoice, one price variance, one quantity variance, and one credit memo.
keyTerms: Evaluated Receipt Settlement: invoice generated from PO and GR

tryIt.task: Run MB5S for your supplier and look for open GR/IR balances.
Set ERS on your supplier and a new PO, post the GR and run MRRL.
Trainer kit: write four invoice-matching exercises (clean, price variance, quantity variance, credit memo).

flashcards: S price: where do PO/standard differences go?
V price: invoice difference with stock on hand goes to…

quiz.q: Which transaction key determines the GR/IR clearing account?
Standard price €10, PO price €12, GR of 10 units. Price differences posted?
With price control V, an invoice price higher than the PO price (stock on hand) is posted to…
quiz.explain: The difference adjusts stock and the moving average price.

quiz.q: The supplier billed €5 too much per unit but quantities are correct. You post a…
quiz.explain: Subsequent credit corrects price without quantity.

quiz.q: An invoice exceeds the price tolerance. What happens?
options: It posts but is blocked for payment
quiz.explain: It posts with payment block R and must be released (MRBR).

quiz.q: Which transaction creates invoices automatically from PO and GR without a paper invoice?
What does a balance on the GR/IR account indicate?
options: Mismatch between goods received and invoiced
quiz.explain: GR/IR shows goods received not invoiced or invoiced not received.
Parked invoices create no accounting document until posted.

howToTeach: Do the S vs V example on paper before any system work
Always open the FI document after MIGO and MIRO
Use one PO to demonstrate clean invoice, variance, block and release
commonMistakes: Using a credit memo for a price correction
Forgetting tax, giving a non-zero balance
Not understanding why GR/IR has a balance at month-end
demoScript: MIGO GR on an S-price material: show PRD
MIRO with a price variance: invoice blocked
